# dreamd — Full Documentation for LLMs
#
# Purpose: Long-form context bundle for AI tools (larger than llms.txt).
# Audience: External LLMs needing install, API, and architecture context.
# Regenerate: Update manually when README, SPEC, or GUIDE change materially.
# Index: see llms.txt for the short link list.

## What dreamd is

dreamd makes Claude Code, Cursor, and Cline remember the same things. Drop a `.agent/`
folder in your repo, run `npx -y dreamd-mcp`, and every MCP-aware coding agent reads and
writes the same memory — episodic events, lessons, preferences — checked into git
alongside your code.

AGENTS.md is what you wrote down. dreamd is what your agent learned, across every tool.

The problem dreamd solves: developers now run 4+ coding agents in rotation. Every one
of them has amnesia about your codebase. Claude Code learns something Tuesday afternoon;
Cursor has no idea Friday morning. dreamd is the fix — a shared memory layer all of them
read and write via MCP, without any of them needing to know the others exist.

## What dreamd is not

- Not a vector database. Recall is BM25 lexical (Tantivy) × salience. Vector/embedding
  and hybrid recall are not shipped. (The "semantic" layer is LESSONS.md indexed as
  documents, scored the same lexical way — not embeddings.)
- Not a hosted SaaS. Memory stays local by default. The only opt-in network path is
  an LLM-assisted dream cycle (API key required; `--no-llm` stays offline).
- Not a replacement for AGENTS.md or SKILL.md. Those are human-authored project rules;
  `.agent/` is machine-written runtime memory. They complement each other.
- Not a Python SDK. No Python required. Distribution is npm (`npx`) and Rust (`cargo`).
- Not an embedded memory SDK. Mem0, Letta, and Zep are libraries you put inside
  one agent you control. dreamd is a folder several existing agents share through
  MCP. Mem0 also speaks MCP; Letta Code is harness-native. The cell-by-cell
  comparison is docs/compared.md.

## Install

### No Rust required (npx path)

  npx -y dreamd-mcp setup   # scaffold .agent/ and wire your harness
  npx -y dreamd-mcp         # start the MCP server (stdio)

Supported: Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/aarch64 (the prebuilt binaries the npm shim
downloads). The shim has no Windows binary. A dreamd.exe from source, or from a
GitHub release's windows-x86_64.tar.gz when that release has one, does watch and
learn over loopback TCP with a bearer token. The dream cycle and the Tantivy
index need Unix atomic writes. Node >= 18 required.

Version note: this describes 1.0.0, published on GitHub as `v1.0.0` and on npm
as `dreamd-mcp` 1.0.0. `blame`, `salience-drift`, `memory`, `forget`,
`recall --without`, `doctor --provenance`, and `explain=1` are in that version.

### From source (requires Rust stable)

  git clone https://github.com/botzrDev/dreamd.git
  cd dreamd
  cargo install --path crates/dreamd-cli
  dreamd setup             # or `dreamd init` to scaffold without writing MCP config
  dreamd mcp

## MCP configuration

`setup` writes this block for you (`.mcp.json` for Claude Code, `.cursor/mcp.json`
for Cursor). By hand:

### Claude Code — add to `.mcp.json` in your project root:

  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "dreamd": {
        "command": "npx",
        "args": ["-y", "dreamd-mcp"]
      }
    }
  }

### Cursor — same block in `.cursor/mcp.json`. Also copy
  `adapters/cursor/.cursor/rules/dreamd-recall.mdc`
  into your project's `.cursor/rules/` for automatic recall on session start.

### Cline / other MCP-aware harnesses — same `mcpServers` block in the harness's
  own MCP settings file (Cline: see adapters/cline/README.md).

## MCP tools

dreamd exposes two MCP tools: `search_nodes` and `append_node`.

### search_nodes — recall from memory

  Input:  { "query": "string", "k": number }   (k defaults to 5; no other arguments)
  Output: { "results": [...] } ranked by BM25 × salience. Each hit has score, bm25,
          salience, source ("episodic" = raw event, "semantic" = LESSONS.md lesson),
          content, and metadata (timestamp_sec, pain, importance, recurrence,
          skill_action, source_harness).

  Use when:
  - Starting a new task in a project worked in before
  - The user references a past decision or problem
  - About to make a choice that may have a documented prior

### append_node — write to memory

  Input:
  {
    "skill_action":   "rust::error_handling::axum_rejection",  // :: -separated, language-first
    "content":        "Axum requires custom Error types to implement IntoResponse.",
    "source_harness": "claude-code",   // required — omitting causes a deserialization error
    "pain":           7.5,             // 0–10, how disruptive if not known (default 5.0)
    "importance":     8.0,             // 0–10, how broadly applicable (default 5.0)
    "client_dedup_key": "axum_requires_custom_error_types_to_implement_intoresponse"
      // optional idempotency key; a repeat call with the same key returns the first id
  }
  Returns: a tool result with { "id": "evt_…", "timestamp": "…", "deduplicated": false }
  after the line is synced to disk. (HTTP `POST /api/v1/learn` returns 201 with the
  same body.) The server mints `id`, `timestamp`, and `schema_version`.

  skill_action convention: language::domain::specific
    rust::error_handling::axum_rejection
    typescript::testing::vitest_async_timeout
    python::deps::virtualenv_activation

PROTOCOL NOTE: after `initialize`, send `notifications/initialized` before calling
tools, as the MCP lifecycle requires. A just-appended node becomes searchable after
the next index commit (up to 5 s); an empty result right after an append is that delay.

## .agent/ folder layout

  .agent/
    episodic/AGENT_LEARNINGS.jsonl   # append-only event log
    semantic/LESSONS.md              # lessons consolidated by the dream cycle
    semantic/recurrence_counts.json  # cluster counts written by the dream cycle
    personal/PREFERENCES.md          # user preferences (never sent to LLM without consent)
    working/WORKSPACE.md             # scratch file; `dreamd reset workspace` re-scaffolds it
    .dreamd/                         # implementation state — gitignored (index, state,
                                     # config.toml, branches/, provenance/, snapshots/)

All files are UTF-8 plaintext. `.agent/` is checked into git. You can cat, grep, and
git diff any file. Durable appends to the JSONL go through `append_node` / the daemon
(single writer), not hand-edits; the dream cycle rewrites LESSONS.md wholesale.

## Episodic record schema (schema_version: "1.0.0")

  {
    "schema_version": "1.0.0",
    "id":             "evt_01M3YEFV3K86X3S7AKJTVERJ0B",   // evt_ + 26-char ULID, server-minted
    "timestamp":      "2026-05-08T10:55:00Z",
    "source_harness": "claude-code",
    "skill_action":   "rust::error_handling::axum_rejection",
    "content":        "Axum requires custom Error types to implement IntoResponse.",
    "pain":           7.5,
    "importance":     8.0,
    "pinned":         false
  }

## CLI commands

  dreamd setup             # scaffold .agent/ (via init) and write the harness MCP config
  dreamd init              # scaffold .agent/ in the current project
  dreamd mcp               # start MCP server over stdio
  dreamd watch             # foreground daemon mode (SIGINT/SIGTERM-graceful)
  dreamd service install|start|restart|status|uninstall   # per-user service running `watch`
  dreamd status            # daemon liveness, project, last dream cycle
  dreamd dream             # run the dream cycle: consolidate episodic → semantic
  dreamd dream --dry       # print the LESSONS.md the cycle would write; writes nothing
  dreamd recall <query>    # ranked search (table); --explain, --without, --without-cluster
  dreamd blame <query>     # which memories drove a query's ranking; --explain, --json
  dreamd score             # top memories by salience, no query
  dreamd salience-drift    # salience distribution and drift vs. 7 days ago; --json
  dreamd memory branch|checkout|branches|delete|diff|bisect   # named memory snapshots
  dreamd forget <evt_id>   # remove one event + the lesson state naming it; --dry-run, --proof <path>
  dreamd doctor            # health check; --repair, --cluster-health, --provenance
  dreamd archive <evt_id> --force-unpin   # clear a pin so decay can prune the entry
  dreamd migrate --from 1.0.0 --to 1.0.0  # episodic schema migration (identity no-op only)
  dreamd vectors enable    # model download on a `--features vectors` build; exits 2 on
                           # the default binary; recall is unchanged either way
  dreamd uninstall         # stop local servers, unregister project, clear caches
  dreamd update            # clear the binary cache so npx fetches the latest
  dreamd version           # structured version output
  dreamd reset workspace   # re-scaffold working/WORKSPACE.md

On the npm path, `npx -y dreamd-mcp <cmd>` forwards init, setup, watch, doctor, dream,
reset, service, uninstall, update, version, mcp, blame, salience-drift, memory, forget,
vectors. recall, score, status, archive, and migrate need the `dreamd` binary.

## HTTP API (daemon)

`dreamd watch` serves HTTP on the Unix socket `~/.agent/dreamd.sock` (peer-UID checked);
every request carries `X-Agent-Root: <project root>`. On Windows it is loopback TCP +
bearer token instead. Main routes: `POST /api/v1/learn`, `GET /api/v1/recall`
(`q`, `k`, `explain=1` for a `citations` array, repeatable `exclude=`),
`POST /api/v1/dream`, `GET /api/v1/health`, `GET /api/v1/preferences`,
`GET /api/v1/observability/salience`. `POST /api/v1/migrate`
is a stub that answers 501. Full reference: docs/http-api.md.

## Recall latency (warm in-RAM BM25 index, Criterion 0.5, WSL2/Linux; historical measurement, not re-run on 1.0.0)

  1,000 entries    ~50 µs
  10,000 entries   ~313 µs
  100,000 entries  ~2.8 ms

All well under the <5ms P50 warm target. Run `cargo bench -p dreamd-core --bench recall` to
reproduce (docs/benchmarks.md).
Read-after-write visibility: up to commit_cadence_seconds (default 5s).

## Privacy

Memory stays local by default. The daemon makes no network calls unless you opt
into an LLM-assisted dream cycle (API key in the environment or
`~/.config/dreamd/secrets.toml`; `--no-llm` keeps the cycle offline).
`.agent/personal/` is excluded from that request unless you pass
`--share-personal` on that call.

## Current scope (v1.0.0)

IN: BM25 lexical recall (including `LESSONS.md` as a Tantivy document layer —
not embeddings), Linux + macOS full daemon, Windows watch+learn, opt-in LLM
dream cycle, `dreamd service`, npm `dreamd-mcp`, memory branches
(`dreamd memory …`), provenance ledger recording + `dreamd doctor --provenance`
(unsigned, no trust label), `dreamd forget` (receipt, not a signed proof),
`dreamd blame`, `recall --without`, `salience-drift`, `explain=1` citations.
NOT: vector/embedding or hybrid recall (the optional `vectors` cargo feature only
downloads a model), Windows atomic writes (dream cycle + index), Homebrew,
auto dream cycle, signed proofs, sync/CRDT.
